title: Unexpected region flapping and policy rollback postmortem
creator: Priya Nair
description: A production incident where rapid latency oscillations in europe-west-2 caused the smart routing system to repeatedly mark the region as draining. The drain policy immediately removed traffic weights and triggered a cascade of fallback model variants and cross-region migrations, creating amplified load on other regions and briefly violating latency SLOs for high-tier customers.
incident_summary: At 02:12 UTC on 2026-02-10 a latency spike in europe-west-2 caused health probes to flip. The routing policy responded by performing an aggressive drain and weight zeroing for that region. Requests were rerouted to cheaper tier variants and then to smaller quantized model variants when capacity remained tight, producing a fallback surge. Multiple downstream autoscalers reacted to the sudden weight shift, scaling nodes in other regions and introducing additional transient capacity loss due to pod churn. The event lasted ~42 minutes; customer-facing errors and increased p99 latencies were observed between 02:15-02:30 UTC.
timeline: 2026-02-10 02:09 UTC - baseline: minor latency variance in eu-west-2 under normal traffic
2026-02-10 02:12 UTC - health probe threshold exceeded by 3 consecutive probes for control plane -> region flagged as degraded
2026-02-10 02:13 UTC - routing policy applied hard drain: region weight set to 0 and active connection termination for in-flight requests
2026-02-10 02:14 UTC - routing engine re-evaluated tier routing: many requests moved to lower-cost tier models due to tier-policy fallback rules
2026-02-10 02:15 UTC - fallback variant depth increased: several requests landed on quantized variants (q4/q3) because preferred variants had no capacity
2026-02-10 02:18 UTC - autoscaler activity spike in us-west-1 and ap-southeast-1; control plane detected scaling churn
2026-02-10 02:23 UTC - partial rollback: ops manually raised eu-west-2 weight to 25% to stabilize traffic while nodes warmed up
2026-02-10 02:35 UTC - routing policy rules adjusted to use soft-drain and sticky-session hints; fallback depth capped at 1
2026-02-10 02:54 UTC - traffic patterns normalized; post-incident monitoring checks green by 03:00 UTC
root_cause: A combination of aggressive hard-drain routing policy (instant weight zeroing + termination of in-flight connections) and the fallback policy that allowed unlimited cascading variant fallbacks. The routing change was pushed in routing-2.3 with a config flag that made drains immediate for faster failover; telemetry and rate-limiting for fallback depth were insufficient. Autoscaler and instance-provision timing interacted poorly with sudden traffic shifts, increasing overall instability.
mitigations_applied_immediate: Manual rollback of the routing policy flag (routing-2.3) in prod to re-enable soft drains
Reintroduced sticky session hints so in-flight connections were preferentially routed back to healthy nodes in eu-west-2
Temporarily capped fallback variant depth to 1 to prevent cascading quality regressions and unpredictable cost spikes
Tuned autoscaler cooldowns to ignore very short-lived weight changes so scale decisions are based on sustained utilization
impact_metrics: Peak fallback rate: 28% of requests used a non-preferred variant between 02:15-02:22 UTC
SLA breaches: two P95 latency SLO violations for enterprise customers (max observed P95 1.8s vs SLO 1.2s)
Error increase: 0.9% client-facing 5xx spike at peak
Cost impact: estimated transient additional serving cost +15% in the affected hour due to cross-region rerouting and scaled instances
long_term_actions: Change routing drain behavior: implement 'soft-drain' by default (weight ramp down over configurable window) and preserve sticky routing for a grace period
Add circuit-breaker for fallback depth: stop automatic fallback after N variant hops and surface alerts to on-call instead of silently degrading quality
Enhance routing telemetry: capture per-request decision trace (region, tier, variant, fallback_depth) and ship to traces with sampling for incident analysis
Canary and sequencing rules: new routing policy flags must pass multi-region canaries and a choreography test that simulates drift and autoscaler interaction
Autoscaler coordination: add a short-term smoothing layer so autoscalers ignore sub-minute weight fluctuations; align scale-up times with routing weight windows
Introduce a routing simulation harness in CI that replays historical traffic with planned policy changes to surface regression risks
Update runbooks and playbooks: new emergency rollback command 'routing rollback soft-drain <policy>' and checklist for fallback-cap capping

SRE review (Ibrahim Coleman): recommend autoscaler cooldown tuning and add a mitigation to avoid simultaneous scale-downs during drains
Design review (Aaron Kim): add UI affordance in Console to preview weight ramp and sticky session behavior before applying policy
Security review (Maya Chen): no direct security risk, advisory to include audits for control-plane changes
notes_and_lessons: Immediate hard-weight removal is brittle when autoscalers and cross-region provisioning are in play; prefer gradual weight-moving with explicit sticky hints
Fallback policies need explicit economic/leakage limits to avoid runaway variant cascades that amplify cost and reduce quality
Operational changes to routing must include traceable per-request decision telemetry and a canary plan that includes autoscaler behavior
Runbooks must include a simple manual knob that ops can hit to cap fallback depth and restore preferred-variant routing while nodes warm up
